name: Pull-Up
instructions: Grip a fixed bar with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width, palms facing away, and hang with arms fully extended.
Set the shoulders by pulling the shoulder blades down and back, and brace your core to stop the body from swinging.
Drive your elbows down toward your ribs and pull until your chin clears the bar.
Pause briefly at the top with the chest lifted toward the bar.
Lower under control until the arms are fully straight again, then repeat.
formCues: Lead with the elbows, not the chin
Keep ribs down and core braced
Control the descent, no dropping
commonMistakes: Kipping or swinging to gain momentum
Using a partial range and not reaching a full hang

name: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit at the machine and secure your thighs under the pads, then grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Sit tall with a slight backward lean and lift the chest toward the bar.
Pull the bar down to your upper chest by driving your elbows down and back.
Squeeze the back at the bottom as the bar reaches the upper chest.
Let the bar rise under control until the arms are fully extended overhead, then repeat.
formCues: Pull to the upper chest, not behind the neck
Drive elbows toward the floor
Keep a tall, stable torso
commonMistakes: Leaning back excessively and using bodyweight to yank the bar
Shrugging the shoulders up instead of pulling the elbows down

name: Barbell Bent-Over Row
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and grip the barbell just outside your knees with an overhand grip.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is around 45 degrees, keeping a flat, neutral spine and soft knees.
Brace your core and pull the bar toward your lower ribs by driving your elbows back.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top without raising your torso.
Lower the bar under control until the arms are straight, then repeat.
formCues: Maintain a flat, neutral spine throughout
Pull to the lower ribs, elbows back
Keep the bar close to the body
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back under load
Using momentum and standing up to heave the weight

name: Single-Arm Dumbbell Row
instructions: Place one knee and the same-side hand on a flat bench, keeping your back flat and roughly parallel to the floor.
Let the dumbbell hang at arm's length from the free hand with the shoulder relaxed into a stretch.
Brace your core and pull the dumbbell toward your hip by driving your elbow up and back.
Squeeze the back at the top, keeping the torso square to the bench.
Lower the dumbbell under control to a full stretch, then repeat before switching sides.
formCues: Keep the back flat and torso steady
Pull the elbow toward the hip
Avoid twisting the torso to lift
commonMistakes: Rotating the torso to swing the weight up
Shrugging the shoulder instead of rowing with the back

name: Seated Cable Row
instructions: Sit at the cable station with feet planted on the platform and knees slightly bent, gripping the handle.
Sit tall with a neutral spine and arms extended, allowing a slight stretch across the shoulder blades.
Pull the handle toward your lower abdomen by driving your elbows back and squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Hold briefly at the contraction with the chest up and torso upright.
Extend the arms under control back to the start without letting the lower back round, then repeat.
formCues: Keep the chest tall and torso upright
Lead with the elbows, squeeze the blades
Control the stretch, don't let the back round
commonMistakes: Leaning far back and rowing with the lower back
Jerking the weight with a heaving torso

name: Conventional Deadlift
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart and the barbell over your mid-foot, close to your shins.
Hinge at the hips and bend the knees to grip the bar just outside your legs, keeping a flat, neutral spine.
Take a breath, brace your core, and pull the slack out of the bar so your lats are tight.
Drive through your heels and extend the hips and knees together, keeping the bar close to your body.
Stand fully upright with shoulders back, then reverse the motion by hinging the hips and lowering the bar under control.
formCues: Keep a flat, neutral spine throughout
Push the floor away and keep the bar against your legs
Lock out by squeezing the glutes, not leaning back
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back during the lift
Letting the bar drift away from the body

name: Dumbbell Pullover
instructions: Lie on a flat bench and hold one dumbbell with both hands cupped under the top plate, arms extended over your chest.
Keep a slight bend in the elbows and brace your core with the ribs down.
Lower the dumbbell in an arc behind your head until you feel a stretch through the lats and chest.
Pull the dumbbell back over your chest by driving with the lats, keeping the elbow angle fixed.
Return to the start position over the chest, then repeat.
formCues: Keep a fixed, slight elbow bend throughout
Feel the stretch through the lats, not the lower back
Keep ribs down and core braced
commonMistakes: Flaring the ribs and arching the lower back at the stretch
Bending and straightening the elbows like a triceps extension

name: Dumbbell Shrug
instructions: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, arms straight and palms facing your thighs.
Brace your core and keep your chin level with the shoulders relaxed down to start.
Elevate the shoulders straight up toward your ears as high as possible.
Pause and squeeze the traps at the top of the movement.
Lower the shoulders under control to a full stretch, then repeat.
formCues: Lift the shoulders straight up, not in circles
Pause and squeeze at the top
Keep the arms straight and relaxed
commonMistakes: Rolling the shoulders, which adds no benefit and stresses the joint
Using too much weight and barely moving the shoulders
